cluster: UN Comtrade API v1 (comtradeapi.un.org) for HS 0409 / 040900 natural honey

sources.name: UN Comtrade API v1: keyed final-data endpoint (data/v1/get)
sources.access_method: REST API (JSON; CSV also selectable via format=CSV)
endpoints: GET https://comtradeapi.un.org/data/v1/get/{typeCode}/{freqCode}/{clCode}?reporterCode=&period=&partnerCode=&partner2Code=&cmdCode=&flowCode=&customsCode=&motCode=&maxRecords=&format=JSON&aggregateBy=&breakdownMode=classic&countOnly=&includeDesc=true   [URL template and query-param names VERIFIED from UN Comtrade's official Python client comtradeapicall 1.3.2, PreviewGet.py]

Path values: typeCode C=goods, S=services; freqCode A=annual, M=monthly; clCode HS (as reported) or a fixed edition H0..H6, S1..S4 (SITC), B4/B5 (BEC)  [C/S, A/M, HS verified in client README; edition codes from memory]

Honey example (monthly, EU+US importers, selected origins + World): https://comtradeapi.un.org/data/v1/get/C/M/HS?reporterCode=380,276,724,842&period=202601,202602,202603&cmdCode=0409&flowCode=M&partnerCode=0,32,156,804,688,76,704,699&partner2Code=0&customsCode=C00&motCode=0&includeDesc=true&maxRecords=100000   with header Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key: <key>

Honey example (annual, exporter side): https://comtradeapi.un.org/data/v1/get/C/A/HS?reporterCode=32,156,804,688,76,704,699&period=2025&cmdCode=040900&flowCode=X&partnerCode=0&includeDesc=true&maxRecords=100000
Count only (to check size before pulling): same URL plus &countOnly=true  -> {"count": N, ...}  [verified: client reads jsonResult['count']]
Key as query param instead of header: ...&subscription-key=<key>  [verified: the official client sends the key this way]

Tariff-line (national 8-10 digit) data: https://comtradeapi.un.org/data/v1/getTariffline/C/{freqCode}/HS?reporterCode=&period=&cmdCode=0409&flowCode=&partnerCode=&partner2Code=&customsCode=&motCode=&maxRecords=&format=JSON&countOnly=&includeDesc=true  [URL verified]

Mirror/bilateral comparison (reported vs partner-reported): https://comtradeapi.un.org/tools/v1/getBilateralData/C/{freqCode}/HS?reporterCode=&period=&cmdCode=&flowCode=&partnerCode=&maxRecords=&format=JSON&includeDesc=  [URL verified; key required]
Trade balance layout: https://comtradeapi.un.org/tools/v1/getTradeBalance/C/{freqCode}/HS?reporterCode=&period=&cmdCode=&partnerCode=&breakdownMode=classic  [URL verified]
Trade Matrix (UNSD estimates, NOT reported stats): https://comtradeapi.un.org/data/v1/getTradeMatrix/C/A/TM?reporterCode=&period=&cmdCode=&flowCode=&partnerCode=  [URL verified]

Premium only: https://comtradeapi.un.org/async/v1/get/C/{freq}/HS (async, up to 2.5M rows, status via https://comtradeapi.un.org/async/v1/getDA/?batchId=) and https://comtradeapi.un.org/bulk/v1/get/C/{freq}/HS (bulk .gz files)  [URLs verified]
sources.auth: Free key. Register at https://comtradedeveloper.un.org (Azure API Management developer portal; sign-up/login with a UN Comtrade account), go to Products, subscribe to the free product named 'comtrade - v1' (name per rOpenSci comtradr docs), then the Profile page shows a Primary and Secondary key (either works). Send it as HTTP header 'Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key: <key>' (standard APIM header, cited in search snippets) or as query param 'subscription-key=<key>' (verified in official client). Premium tiers (bulk/async, higher limits) are paid via subscriptions@un.org.
sources.cost_licensing: Free tier: no cost. Terms (from search snippets; the live uncomtrade.org terms page could not be fetched from this sandbox, so re-read it before go-live): UN Comtrade data are UN copyright. Internal analysis is allowed. Re-dissemination, meaning re-publishing the data as-is in another platform, needs an active Premium Pro subscription. Exceptions listed on the UN shop page: small extracts (up to 100,000 records) and free public visualisations. The legacy licence (comtrade.un.org/licenseagreement.html) bars automated browsing or downloading of the website and commercial redistribution without permission (contact comtrade@un.org). So use the API with a key and do not scrape the comtradeplus.un.org UI. For a single-PC internal app that shows derived unit values and charts, the risk is low. Do not resell or export the raw datasets to customers. Attribute the data as 'Source: UN Comtrade'.
sources.update_frequency: Continuous, rolling. Each reporter-period dataset is published when the country submits it and UNSD processes it. Past periods are revised and republished. There is no fixed calendar. Use getDa or getLiveUpdate (see the availability source) to detect new or revised releases.
sources.data_available: Rows are reporter x partner x HS code x flow x period, plus partner2, customs procedure and mode of transport. Values are in USD: primaryValue, which is CIF for imports and FOB for exports, plus separate cifvalue and fobvalue. Quantities: netWgt in kg, qty in the qtyUnitCode unit (for honey qtyUnitCode 8 = kg, so qty is usually equal to netWgt), and grossWgt (often empty). There is no variety breakdown: HS 0409 / 040900 'Natural honey' covers every floral type. The tariff-line endpoint gives national 8-10 digit splits where the reporter provides them (for example, US HTS splits honey by colour grade; from memory). Annual (A) and monthly (M) frequencies are available. Monthly coverage is thinner because many reporters send only annual data. Prices must be derived: unit value = primaryValue / netWgt, in USD/kg.
sources.parsing_notes: 1) Response envelope: data rows are in top-level 'data' (array) and the total in 'count' (both verified in the official client). 'elapsedTime' (string such as '0.31 secs') and 'error' (string, empty when OK) are from memory. Check HTTP status first: Azure APIM gives 401 for a missing or invalid key, 429 when the rate limit is exceeded ('Try again in N seconds'), and 403 when the daily quota is exhausted (APIM messages from memory). 2) Truncation: if len(data) == maxRecords, the result was cut off, so split by reporter or period. Use countOnly=true to size a query first. 3) Avoid double counting. partnerCode 0 = World total, so never add it to the per-partner rows. Area or group partner codes can also appear; drop them using isGroup from the partner reference file. Ask for breakdownMode=classic (the client's default) and also pin partner2Code=0, customsCode=C00 and motCode=0. In 'plus' mode one partner can return several rows split by customs procedure or mode of transport. 4) cmdCode 0409 (4-digit) and 040900 (6-digit) carry the same values, because 0409 has only one subheading. Query only one of them. aggrLevel is 4 or 6. 5) With clCode=HS, rows come in the reporter's original edition, shown in classificationCode ('H5' for 2017-21, 'H6' for 2022+), and classificationSearchCode='HS'. Honey's code has not changed across editions, so no concordance is needed. 6) Nulls: on imports fobvalue is often null and on exports cifvalue is often null, so use primaryValue. netWgt can be null or 0. isNetWgtEstimated / isQtyEstimated = true means UNSD estimated the weight; flag those unit values or drop them. Guard against division by 0. 7) With includeDesc=false the *Desc and *ISO fields come back null (memory), so always send includeDesc=true or join the reference tables. 8) period is 'YYYY' (annual) or 'YYYYMM' (monthly). Several values are comma-separated. The comtradr docs say a monthly query is limited to 12 months, so stay within 12 periods per call. refPeriodId looks like YYYYMMDD (e.g. 20230101). Annual rows carry refMonth=52 (memory). Store period as a string. 9) Multi-value params (reporterCode, partnerCode, cmdCode, flowCode, period) are comma-separated. Param-name case appears not to matter: the official client sends 'reportercode' in lower case. Use the documented camelCase. 10) Flow codes: M=Import, X=Export, RM=Re-import, RX=Re-export; there are other extended codes. 11) Comtrade country codes differ from ISO numeric for some countries: USA=842 (not 840), France=251, India=699, Switzerland=757, Norway=579. Taiwan appears only as partner 490 'Other Asia, nes' (memory; check in partnerAreas.json). Codes for this app: Italy 380, Germany 276, Spain 724, Belgium 56, UK 826, Poland 616, Japan 392, Saudi Arabia 682, China 156, Argentina 32, Brazil 76, Ukraine 804, Serbia 688, Viet Nam 704, Mexico 484, Uruguay 858, Türkiye 792, Romania 642, Hungary 348, Moldova 498, Bulgaria 100, New Zealand 554, Canada 124. Resolve them from Reporters.json rather than hard-coding. 12) Revisions: re-pull the last 24 months each run and upsert on (typeCode, freqCode, period, reporterCode, flowCode, partnerCode, partner2Code, cmdCode, customsCode, motCode). 13) Mirror asymmetry: importer CIF figures and exporter FOB figures will not match, because of freight, timing and origin-versus-consignment rules. Keep the reporter side as a dimension.
sources.publication_lag: From memory, unverified: annual data for large reporters usually appear 6-12 months after year-end, and full coverage takes 18 months or more. Monthly data from prompt reporters (EU members, US, China, Brazil and others) usually lag 2-4 months. Many origin countries never send monthly data. As of 2026-11-02, expect annual 2025 for the main reporters and monthly through about mid-2026 for EU/US reporters. Check per reporter with getDa.
sources.rate_limits: Free key: 500 calls/day and up to 100,000 records per call (rOpenSci comtradr docs, citing UN). Search snippets citing the UN subscription page give 1 call/second on Free and 5 calls/second on Premium. Note that the official client README describes getFinalData as 'limited to 250K records', which may be a premium or newer cap; treat 100,000 as the safe free maximum. Quota reset time is not documented in what I could read. Throttle to at most 1 request per 1.1 s and back off on 429/403.

sources.honey_specific_codes: HS 0409 = 'Natural honey'. Its only HS6 subheading is 040900, so use cmdCode=0409 or cmdCode=040900, not both. Related codes you may want: 0410 (insects and other edible animal products, n.e.s.; in HS2022 this includes royal jelly), 1521.90 (beeswax), 0106.41 (bees, HS2022). Quantity unit qtyUnitCode 8 = kg (the SUV example in the official client uses qtyUnitCode=8 for kg). partnerCode 0 = World.

sources.cost_licensing: Free and needs no account. The same UN Comtrade terms apply as for the keyed endpoint: internal use is fine; re-dissemination of the raw data needs Premium Pro unless the extract is small (100,000 records or fewer) or a free public visualisation (UN shop page snippet).
sources.update_frequency: Same underlying database as data/v1/get (rolling releases).
sources.data_available: The same record schema as the keyed endpoint, capped at 500 rows per call. That is enough for honey: one reporter x one period x one flow returns roughly 10-80 partner rows. Some third-party wrappers note that the preview can return empty results for certain reporter/period combinations (search snippet).
sources.parsing_notes: Same envelope and fields as data/v1/get. The official client's _previewFinalData helper splits a comma-separated period list into one call per period. Do the same: one reporter and one period per call keeps you safely under 500 rows. If len(data)==500, assume truncation and narrow the query, for example by adding partnerCode. Throttle conservatively (about 1 call every 2 s). The exact preview rate limit is not documented in what I could read, and snippets only say it is 'rate-limited'. Treat empty 'data' as 'not yet reported' and cross-check with public/v1/getDa.
sources.publication_lag: Same as the keyed endpoint (see above).
sources.rate_limits: 500 records per call (verified: the official client README says 'limited to 500 records'). Calls per day are described as unlimited but rate-limited (third-party snippet); the exact per-second limit is unverified.
sources.sample_response: Same structure as the data/v1/get sample: {"elapsedTime":..., "count": N, "data": [ {typeCode, freqCode, refPeriodId, refYear, refMonth, period, reporterCode, reporterISO, reporterDesc, flowCode, flowDesc, partnerCode, partnerISO, partnerDesc, partner2Code, ..., cmdCode, cmdDesc, qtyUnitCode, qtyUnitAbbr, qty, netWgt, cifvalue, fobvalue, primaryValue, isReported, isAggregate} ], "error": ""}. sources.update_frequency: Rarely, when codes or country lists change. Re-download monthly and cache locally.
sources.data_available: Comtrade reporter and partner area codes with names, ISO2/ISO3 codes, whether each entry is a group, and validity dates. Also the HS code tree with descriptions, the ISO3-to-code map and country group definitions (EU, LDC and so on).
sources.parsing_notes: Every file wraps rows in 'results' (verified for ListofReferences.json, country_area_code_iso.json and country_groups.json; the official client also notes the files may carry a UTF-8 BOM and decodes them as 'utf-8-sig'). Decode with utf-8-sig, or strip the BOM, before calling json.loads. From memory, unverified: Reporters.json rows look like {id, text, reporterCode, reporterDesc, reporterNote, reporterCodeIsoAlpha2, reporterCodeIsoAlpha3, entryEffectiveDate, entryExpiredDate, isGroup}. partnerAreas.json uses CAPITALISED keys {id, text, PartnerCode, PartnerDesc, partnerNote, PartnerCodeIsoAlpha2, PartnerCodeIsoAlpha3, entryEffectiveDate, isGroup}, with World = id 0, ISO 'W00'. Match keys case-insensitively. A third-party MCP module reads reporterCodeIsoAlpha2/3 from Reporters.json (snippet), which partly confirms those names. Some codes are historical, such as former Sudan or the Serbia-and-Montenegro era codes; filter on the entry/expiry dates. Not every partner is a reporter: World (0) cannot report.
sources.rate_limits: None documented; cache locally and fetch rarely.

recommendation:
Integrate in this order:

(1) One-off and monthly: cache the reference tables. Start from https://comtradeapi.un.org/files/v1/app/reference/ListofReferences.json and follow its fileuri links for the 'reporter' and 'partner' categories. Decode with utf-8-sig and match keys case-insensitively. Build a local table of Comtrade country codes; watch USA=842, France=251, India=699, and Taiwan appearing as 490.

(2) Ship the keyless public preview first. Use https://comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/preview/C/{A|M}/HS with cmdCode=0409, partner2Code=0, customsCode=C00, motCode=0 and includeDesc=true, one reporter and one period per call. Pull imports (flowCode=M) for the destination markets: Italy 380, Germany 276, Spain 724, Belgium 56, France 251, UK 826, USA 842, Japan 392, Saudi Arabia 682. Pull exports (flowCode=X) for the origins: Argentina 32, China 156, Ukraine 804, Serbia 688, Brazil 76, Viet Nam 704, India 699, Mexico 484, Uruguay 858, Türkiye 792. Each call returns about 10-80 rows, well under the 500-row cap. Compute unit value as primaryValue / netWgt (USD/kg). Exclude partner 0 (World) from sums, and flag rows where isNetWgtEstimated is true.

(3) Register a free key at comtradedeveloper.un.org: subscribe to the 'comtrade - v1' product and send the key in the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header. Then switch to https://comtradeapi.un.org/data/v1/get/C/{freq}/HS, putting several reporters and up to 12 periods in one call with maxRecords up to 100000. Throttle to 1 call per second or slower and back off on 429/403. The whole honey panel fits in a handful of calls per run, far below 500 calls/day.

(4) Drive refreshes from https://comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/getDa/C/M/HS?publishedDateFrom=... (no key needed), so you only re-pull reporter-periods that are new or revised. Also re-pull the trailing 24 months weekly, and upsert on (freq, period, reporter, flow, partner, partner2, cmd, customs, mot).

(5) Optional: add getSUV (cmdCode=040900, qtyUnitCode=8) as a global USD/kg benchmark once you have a key, but inspect its fields live first.

Schedule weekly. Comtrade lags by months (annual about 6-12+ months, monthly about 2-4 months for EU/US/China), so position it as the structural, mirror-checked origin-price layer, not a spot-price feed. Pair it with faster national monthly sources (Eurostat Comext CN 04090000, US Census/USITC HTS 0409) from the other clusters.

Keep the extracts internal. Re-publishing raw Comtrade data outside the company needs Premium Pro, apart from the small-extract and free-visualisation exceptions.

Verification caveat: comtradedeveloper.un.org and uncomtrade.org were blocked by this sandbox's network policy. To read the official doc pages directly, add those domains to the session's network settings. URL templates and query-param names were instead verified from UN Comtrade's own Python client (comtradeapicall 1.3.2 on PyPI, github.com/uncomtrade/comtradeapicall). Response field names come from the rOpenSci comtradr field mapping and from memory, so the developer should log the first live response and confirm the field list before locking the parser. The official client itself (pip install comtradeapicall, which needs pandas and urllib3) is a usable fallback, but plain httpx calls to the templates above are simpler for a scheduled collector.
